A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Daze study and contain complete, readable main text, figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–E. All 28 pages can be reliably compared.

before.justification: v1 reports original MuJoCo and Atari experiments, physical robot demonstrations, and additional TD3/DQN evaluations and parameter ablations in Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results, including attack-success and benign-return measurements, robot action histograms and appendix ablations.

M1.justification: Daze's transition rules, trigger/daze mechanisms and Algorithm 1 are unchanged. Section 3.3's revised wrapper explanation does not introduce or modify an algorithmic component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same three MuJoCo tasks, four Atari games, and Intersection and Waiter scenarios, including physical robot tests. The appendices add no coverage relative to v1.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains TrojDRL-C and SleeperNets-C for continuous-control comparisons; Table 2 retains Q-Incept, TrojDRL and SleeperNets for discrete PPO comparisons. Unpoisoned controls and appendix comparator membership are unchanged.

E3.justification: ASR/BR definitions, training budgets, preprocessing, trigger configurations and poisoning settings remain unchanged in Section 4 and Appendix C. No evaluation procedure is added or revised.

E4.justification: The Hopper poisoning-rate/daze-factor ablations in Tables 5–6, robot behavior analyses and additional TD3/DQN evaluations are retained without changes. No robustness test or supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same averaging over 100 trajectories and five training seeds, standard deviations, and two-run descriptions for the physical-robot histograms. No uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Main results in Tables 1–2, appendix results in Tables 3–6, daze rates in Table 8 and physical-robot findings are unchanged. No scores, result entries, rankings or qualitative outcomes are revised.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Assumption 1, Theorems 1–2 and Appendix E proofs are unchanged. The spacing adjustment around the threshold inequality on page 6 has no mathematical effect.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about reward-free simulator backdoors, theoretical success/stealth guarantees, empirical effectiveness and transfer to robotic hardware.

C2.justification: Section 3.3's added sentence about hiding the attack within domain randomization reiterates discussion already present in v1 Section 5 and Appendix D.1. Interpretations, applicability qualifications and defense limitations are otherwise unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 4.2 and the reproducibility statement replace anonymous supplement links with links to the authors' named GitHub repository. Implementation and hyperparameter disclosures are unchanged; Appendix C.5 still retains its anonymous link.

R1.justification: The cited-work set and research positioning remain unchanged. The added Tobin et al. citation in Section 3.3 references work already cited for the same domain-randomization argument elsewhere in v1.

P1.justification: v3 locally rewrites Section 3.3 and supplement-access wording, adds funding acknowledgments as Section 7, and renumbers the ethics and reproducibility statements. The overall narrative and appendix structure remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 fixes overlapping paragraphs in Section 4.3 on page 9 and makes small spacing and reflow adjustments around Algorithm 1 and the references. Figures and tables retain their content and design.

improvement.justification: v3 improves readability by fixing overlapping text on page 9 and modestly improves transparency through funding acknowledgments and named repository links. These are limited presentation and documentation gains; the methods, evidence and proofs, including the appendices, are unchanged. The access-link update remains incomplete because Appendix C.5 retains anonymous-hosting wording and its old link.
